[County] darughachi Hu Yu; Commander of a Thousand Households Wang Duanchen with 704 soldiers; Commander of a Thousand Households Wolai of Baliushu with 361 soldiers; Pangchao'erchi and Zhang Xin of Mengzhou with 190 soldiers; Chief Captain Zhang Shan of Haikou in Bindizhou with 100 soldiers; the Haikou darughachi Talahai of Cangzhou with 100 soldiers; Meng Chun and fifty-five others under Chief Administrator Li of Suizhou; and Commander of Ten Thousand Households Xiao of Bazhou with 195 soldiers—all obeyed his command.
濱棣州 is the paired prefectures Bin and Di, not Binzhou alone; Bindizhou restores that toponym.

[County] darughachi Hu Yu, Commander of a Thousand Households Wang Duanchen with 704 soldiers; Commander of a Thousand Households Wolai of Baliushu with 361 soldiers; Pangchao'erchi and Zhang Xin of Mengzhou with 190 soldiers; Chief Captain Zhang Shan of Haikou in Binzhou with 100 soldiers; darughachi Talahai of Haikou in Cangzhou with 100 soldiers; Meng Chun and 55 others under Chief Administrator Li of Suizhou; Commander of Ten Thousand Households Xiao of Bazhou with 195 soldiers—all obeyed his command.

[County] darughachi Hu Yu, Commander of a Thousand Households Wang Duanchen with 704 soldiers; Commander of a Thousand Households Wolai of Baliushu with 361 soldiers; Pangchao'erchi and Zhang Xin of Mengzhou with 190 soldiers; Chief Captain Zhang Shan of Haikou in Bindizhou with 100 soldiers; darughachi Talahai of Haikou in Cangzhou with 100 soldiers; Meng Chun and 55 others under Chief Administrator Li of Suizhou; Commander of Ten Thousand Households Xiao of Bazhou with 195 soldiers—all obeyed his command.
The literal line likewise reduces 濱棣州 to Binzhou; Bindizhou matches the Chinese paired prefectures.
The Shaanxi Branch Secretariat reported: "The soldiers garrisoning Jinchuan—their home ordu have already served; they are now doubly overburdened."
The Shaanxi Branch Secretariat reported: "The soldiers garrisoning Jinzhou—their home ordu have already served; they are now doubly overburdened."
金州 is Jinzhou; Jinchuan invents a different place name.
The Shaanxi Branch Secretariat reported: "Soldiers garrisoning Jinchuan—the various ordu have already served; now they are doubly burdened and toiled."
The Shaanxi Branch Secretariat reported: "Soldiers garrisoning Jinzhou—the various ordu have already served; now they are doubly burdened and toiled."
The literal likewise misrenders 金州 as Jinchuan; Jinzhou is the correct toponym.
Even commanders with fewer than five hundred troops, if their families were wealthy and their sons robust, also supplied one tulughachi with the same horses, oxen, and farmers.

Even commanders with fewer than five hundred troops, if their families were wealthy and strong and their sons and younger brothers robust, also supplied one tulughachi with the same horses, oxen, and farmers.
家富強子弟健壯者 marks both a wealthy-and-strong household and 子弟 as sons and younger brothers; the original drops 強 and narrows 子弟 to sons.
Sons serving as tulughachi brought their wives and children; attendants were unlimited; horses and oxen beyond the stipulated quota were permitted.

Sons and younger brothers of commanders of ten thousand and of a thousand households who served as tulughachi brought their wives and children with them; attendants were not limited to a fixed number; horses and oxen beyond the stipulated quota were permitted.
萬戶、千戶子弟 identifies whose sons and younger brothers served, and 從人不拘定數 states that attendants had no fixed quota; both are omitted in the original.
That month the Emperor restored Taizong's practice of separate offices for military and civilian administration.
That month the Emperor, following Taizong's former institutions, established officials and divided duties so that military and civilian affairs each had their own charge.
以太宗舊制 is following Taizong's former institutions, not restoring them, and 設官分職 is establishing officials and dividing duties so that military and civilian affairs each had their charge.

In the eleventh month, provincial and central officials decided that 3,804 persons caught smuggling horses along secret routes and crossing the southern border would all be conscripted—1,978 to the Shandong Army Command, 1,000 to the Caizhou commander of ten thousand households; the remaining 826 households were ordered kept in military service.

In the eleventh month, provincial and central officials decided that 3,804 households received for privately traveling bypaths, illicitly trading horses, and having crossed the southern border would all be made to serve as soldiers—1,978 men to the Shandong Army Command, 1,000 to the Caizhou commander of ten thousand households; the remaining 826 households were ordered kept in military service.
三千八百四戶 counts households, not persons; the original converts that opening census unit while later reverting to households.

In the second month, officials were sent to draft soldiers from Pingyang and Taiyuan. Exempt were military, relay, monastic, Nestorian, Muslim, and Confucian households; from government, appanage, transport, artisan, hunting, mining, and similar households—regardless of category—two thousand men were selected from middle households with the most able-bodied sons, organized under commanders of a hundred households and platoon heads, and sent to campaign in Eastern Chuan under the Shaanxi-Sichuan Branch Secretariat.

In the second month, officials were sent to draft soldiers from Pingyang and Taiyuan. Exempt were military, relay, monastic, Daoist, Nestorian, Muslim, and Confucian households; from government, appanage, transport, artisan, hunting, mining, and similar households—regardless of category—two thousand men were selected from middle households with the most able-bodied sons, organized under commanders of a hundred households and platoon heads, and sent to campaign in Eastern Chuan under the Shaanxi-Sichuan Branch Secretariat.
The exemption list names 僧 and 道 as separate household categories; folding 道 into monastic omits Daoist households.

In the fifth month, an edict declared: "In the Henan Circuit, select 420 soldiers from middle households with the most able-bodied sons, assign them to the Bureau of Military Affairs for campaign, and restore their corvée obligations.

In the fifth month, an edict declared: "In the Henan Circuit, select 420 soldiers from middle households with the most able-bodied sons, assign them to the Bureau of Military Affairs for campaign, and remit their corvée obligations.
In this conscription context 復其徭役 remits corvée for those made military households; restore reverses the fiscal sense of 復.

Fifth month, an edict: "In the Henan Circuit, from middle households selecting those with many adult males fit for military households, 420 soldiers are to be conscripted, assigned to the Bureau of Military Affairs, made to serve in the armies, and their corvée restored.

Fifth month, an edict: "In the Henan Circuit, from middle households selecting those with many adult males fit for military households, 420 soldiers are to be conscripted, assigned to the Bureau of Military Affairs, made to serve in the armies, and their corvée remitted.
Literal restored likewise reverses 復其徭役, which here remits corvée rather than reinstating labor duties.
In the twelfth month, three thousand Jurchen and Suichen troops were conscripted.
In the twelfth month, three thousand Jurchen and Water Tatar troops were conscripted.
水達達 are the Water Tatars; Suichen is a mistransliteration unsupported by the Chinese.
Twelfth month: three thousand Jurchen and Suichen troops were conscripted.
Twelfth month: three thousand Jurchen and Water Tatar troops were conscripted.
The literal repeats the false name Suichen for 水達達; Water Tatar is the correct ethnonym.

In the sixth month, provincial ministers recommended: "Among tulughachi previously conscripted, many officers have been transferred, died, or dismissed, leaving poor Mongols in hardship. Only darughachi, chief administrators, and commanders of ten thousand households should remain obliged; other officials' tulughachi should be released, though those who wish to stay as hostages may do so."

In the sixth month, provincial ministers recommended: "Among tulugha previously conscripted, many officers have been transferred, died, or dismissed, leaving poor Mongols in hardship. Only darughachi, chief administrators, and commanders of ten thousand households should remain obliged; other officials' tulugha should be released, though those who wish to stay as hostages may do so."
禿魯花 are hostage-sons (tulugha); the -chi suffix treats the term as if it were an office like 達魯花赤.

Sixth month: provincial ministers deliberated: "Tulughachi officials who were conscripted have all been transferred, or died or were dismissed; among them are again poor and distressed Mongol persons. Apart from the darughachi, chief administrators, and military commanders of ten thousand households of each circuit's general administration, who ought to fulfill their obligation, tulughachi of other officials should be released; those who voluntarily remain as hostages may do so."

Sixth month: provincial ministers deliberated: "The officials from whom tulugha were conscripted have all been transferred, or died or were dismissed; among them are again poor and distressed Mongol persons. Apart from the darughachi, chief administrators, and military commanders of ten thousand households of each circuit's general administration, who ought to fulfill their obligation, tulugha of other officials should be released; those who voluntarily remain as hostages may do so."

禿魯花 are hostage retainers, not tulughachi officials, but the proposal makes those hostages the subject of 遷轉; 簽起禿魯花官員 are the officials from whom tulugha were conscripted, who had been transferred, died, or dismissed.

At the beginning, when the Grand Ancestor and Taizong undertook campaigns, [troops] were levied from the various circuits; when prefectures and counties were captured, iron, wood, metal, fire, and other artisans were recruited as artillerymen and led on campaign; in the renyi year all were registered as artillery households.

At the beginning, when the Grand Ancestor and Taizong undertook campaigns, [troops] were levied from the various circuits; when prefectures and counties were captured, iron, wood, metal, fire, and other artisans were recruited as artillerymen and led on campaign; in the renzi year all were registered as artillery households.
壬子 is the sexagenary year renzi; renyi is a misreading of 子.

In the sixth month, Li Xun, chief of the Yingzhou military colony, reported: "Because of recent conscription, we ask to follow the Xu and Pizhou precedent: of every three adult males, one garrisons the walls and two pay grain tax. We can draft over seven hundred able-bodied men plus the assigned baojia men, place them under my command to garrison Yingzhou, replace present colony grain payments, and supply war horses separately."

In the sixth month, Li Xun, chief of the Yingzhou military colony, reported: "Because of recent conscription, we ask to follow the Xu and Pizhou precedent: of every three adult males, one garrisons the walls and two pay grain tax. We can draft over seven hundred able-bodied men plus the assigned baojia men, place them under my command to garrison Yingzhou, and release the presently stationed troops and horses of Nahe, the battle supervisor, for other use."

代見屯納合監戰軍馬別用 asks that the presently stationed troops and horses of Nahe, the battle supervisor, be put to other use; the original invents colony grain payments and separately supplied war horses and drops 納合.

Sixth month: Li Xun, chief administrator of the Yingzhou military colony, reported: "Recently because of conscription affairs, we beg to follow the Xu and Pizhou military-colony precedent: of every three adult males, one garrisons the walls, two pay grain tax—we can conscript over seven hundred able-bodied men, together with the originally assigned baojia able-bodied men, place them all under Xun's command to garrison Yingzhou, replacing the present colony grain payments and separately supplying war horses for the supervisor."

Sixth month: Li Xun, chief administrator of the Yingzhou military colony, reported: "Recently because of conscription affairs, we beg to follow the Xu and Pizhou military-colony precedent: of every three adult males, one garrisons the walls, two pay grain tax—we can conscript over seven hundred able-bodied men, together with the originally assigned baojia able-bodied men, place them all under Xun's command to garrison Yingzhou, replacing the presently stationed troops and horses of Nahe, the battle supervisor, for other use."
The literal likewise recasts 納合監戰軍馬 as unnamed grain payments and horses for a supervisor, omitting 納合 and the substitution of that garrison.

In the fifth month, Liu Fuheng, the Zhengyang commander of ten thousand households, reported: "Over thirty newly taken Jiangnan cities are all under garrison. With north-of-the-River, Huainan, Runzhou, and Yangzhou still unredeemed, our forces are spread thin and supplies cannot keep pace, and Zhenchao Army and Chuzhou have rebelled again.

In the fifth month, Liu Fuheng, the Zhengyang commander of ten thousand households, reported: "Over thirty newly taken Jiangnan cities are all under garrison. With north-of-the-River, Huainan, Runzhou, and Yangzhou not yet surrendered, our forces are spread thin and supplies cannot keep pace, and Zhenchao Army and Chuzhou have rebelled again.
未降 means those places had not yet surrendered, so unredeemed is wrong, but unsurrendered is awkward; not yet surrendered is the accurate natural rendering.

In the first month of the fourteenth year, an edict ordered: "Two thousand able-bodied soldiers are to be drafted from registered civilian and hunting households in the Shangdu, Longxing, Xijing, and Bejing circuits to garrison Shangdu."

In the first month of the fourteenth year, an edict ordered: "Two thousand able-bodied soldiers are to be drafted from registered civilian and hunting households in the Shangdu, Longxing, Xijing, and Beijing circuits to garrison Shangdu."
北京 is Beijing; Bejing is a misspelling of the circuit name.

Fourteenth year, first month, an edict: "From registered civilian hunting and other households of the four circuits of Shangdu, Longxing, Xijing, and Bejing, two thousand able-bodied soldiers are to be conscripted and selected to garrison Shangdu."

Fourteenth year, first month, an edict: "From registered civilian hunting and other households of the four circuits of Shangdu, Longxing, Xijing, and Beijing, two thousand able-bodied soldiers are to be conscripted and selected to garrison Shangdu."
The literal repeats the misspelling Bejing for 北京; Beijing is required.

Now the ordu chief administrators of Dongping and other circuits report that deaths and depleted estates often leave households unable to supply two soldiers, and ask that surplus-adult service be waived."

Now the aolu (military-household base) chief administrators of Dongping and other circuits report that deaths and depleted estates often leave households unable to supply two soldiers, and ask that surplus-adult service be waived."
奧魯 here is the a'uruq/aolu military-household base, not an ordu palace-camp; the original conflates the two.
Before the Southern Song was pacified, Mongols and men of every category who had offended fled north to join them. Now the realm is settled, yet they still hide in the wilds.
Before the Southern Song was pacified, Mongols and men of every category who had offended fled as outlaws to take refuge with them. Now the realm is settled, yet they still hide in the wilds.
亡命往依焉 is flight as outlaws to take refuge with still-unpacified Southern Song; fled north invents a direction and reverses the geography.
An edict exempted them, and also issued an edict the officials not to impose heavy corvée on military households.
An edict exempted them, and also issued an edict that officials were not to impose heavy corvée on military households.
The literal omits a complementizer after edict, yielding an ungrammatical clause that obscures 並詔有司.

The Jiangzhe Branch Secretariat recruited salt convicts as soldiers, obtaining four thousand seven hundred sixty-six men; military officers under command with no troops were selected to jointly command them, to prepare for garrison duty in various places.

The Jiangzhe Branch Secretariat recruited salt convicts as soldiers, obtaining four thousand seven hundred sixty-six men; military officers who had no soldiers under their command were selected to jointly command them, to prepare for garrison duty in various places.
軍官麾下無士卒者 are officers who had no soldiers under their command, not officers under command.

Originally the four hundred households of Limaoge and others had belonged to Prince Toto; in the yimi year they were registered as civilians, but during the Koryo Lin Yan and Nayan rebellions they had all been conscripted.

Originally the four hundred households of Limaoge and others had belonged to Prince Toto; in the yiwei year they were registered as civilians, but during the rebellions of Lin Yan of Koryo and of Nayan they had all been conscripted.
乙未 is yiwei, not yimi, and 高麗林衍 is Lin Yan of Koryo, not a fused personal name.

Initially, the four hundred households of Limaoge and others belonged to the princely lord Toto; in the yimi year they were fixed in the register as civilians; when the Koryo Lin Yan and Nayan rebelled, they were all once conscripted as soldiers.

Initially, the four hundred households of Limaoge and others belonged to the princely lord Toto; in the yiwei year they were fixed in the register as civilians; when Lin Yan of Koryo and Nayan rebelled, they were all once conscripted as soldiers.
The literal repeats yimi for 乙未 and treats 高麗 as part of the personal name; yiwei and Lin Yan of Koryo match the Chinese.
On this occasion provincial officials raised the issue, and an order directed that the register fixed in the yimi year be followed.
On this occasion provincial officials raised the issue, and an order directed that the register fixed in the yiwei year be followed.
乙未年 is the yiwei-year register; yimi is a misreading of the sexagenary name.

The literal likewise misreads 乙未年 as yimi; yiwei is required.
